purpose: Validate real window capture, bounded visual region permutation and inverse interaction mapping without modifying source application code.

entities.role: Microsoft Windows.Graphics.Capture and Windows.UI.Composition Win32 sample, MIT-licensed reference

activities.label: compile the isolated native capture sandbox with the official Microsoft CppWinRT package
capture a self-created source window, permute regions, route an internal proxy click and verify the changed frame
reject non-bijective maps, out-of-surface points and unsafe external-window capabilities
record the proxy renderer decision and its limits

queries.expression: can an explicitly self-created window produce a changed captured frame without screen-wide capture
can four visual regions be rearranged while preserving pixel identity at declared destinations
does an interaction on a rearranged region map back to its source region when the map is bijective
does the renderer reject ambiguous maps and external input capabilities

assumptions: The native sandbox owns both the source and proxy HWNDs.
A quadrant permutation is a sufficient minimal test of a reversible spatial transform.
The source window remains visible long enough for Windows.Graphics.Capture to deliver frames.
The official Microsoft sample and CppWinRT package are implementation references, not semantic authorities.
kill_tests: The proxy does not target external windows or inject system input.
A static source does not cause a continuous presentation loop.
A source update that does not reach the proxy is a timeout/failure.
unknowns: Whether the same capture path behaves acceptably for arbitrary user-selected applications.
Whether cross-process input routing can be made safe for UIA-supported controls.
How much latency and GPU cost a GPU-native region compositor adds at sustained updates.
Whether UIA or OCR can identify semantic regions without false reordering.
